ASTERION REACH · INDEPENDENT MILITARY UI PLAYTEST

Iron Covenant

A failed first invasion became a cycle 57 Domination victory. Production timing, negotiated peace, forward repairs and concentrated fleets made the difference.

Outcome and limits

The Concord captured Veyr Prime on cycle 46, Kharos on 53 and Lumen on 57. The last capture immediately ended the game with Domination: 745 legacy points, 104 population and 11 technologies. The final treasury held 2,892 credits and 1,005 minerals; five cruisers and ten frigates remained. No Asterion Beacon was built by the player. Lumen’s existing beacon was captured with the capital.

The Choir began its public alignment on cycle 56 and reached 2/10 before Lumen fell. This was an intervention against an emerging race, not a last-cycle rescue. The victory does not establish that military play is universally stronger than transcendence: it is one deliberately aggressive campaign on one seed, using ordinary rules and visible information.

What was actually played

The opening plan used productive colonies and research to assemble a concentrated frigate fleet, with trade protecting a second frontier. All gameplay mutations were actual clicks or inputs in the frozen browser. No grants, console commands, save edits or rollback were used. A read-only projection exposed only our assets, charted geography, remembered native survey facts, contacted public beacon signals and fleets under local sensors. Raw exported saves were not read for decisions; full-state inspection began only after the victory.

Actual UI exports were retained at cycles 1, 10, 20, 29, 30, 36, 39, 40, 42, 46, 50, 55 and 57. The two cycle-50 export events contain the same state. The opening browser disconnected after three commands; the persistent browser replayed the identical three commands on the same seed before continuing. A cycle-31 process interruption resumed the normal autosave. Neither changed the strategy or campaign state.

The frozen build reports 60fd9f8e85edfee92ed40ee29c9b8c314e140da3, built 2026-10-28T21:00:47.386Z. The game never received later Hold/Resume, diplomacy or combat changes during this run.

The campaign’s turning points

1–12 · Build a base

Sundrift was settled on cycle 1, Ashfall on 12. The ancient escort Last Light of Sundrift was chosen instead of 85 minerals. An archive’s 50 science accelerated Logistics. The second Colony Ark took several cycles to build and several more to reach its destination: production and travel were both genuine commitments.

19–29 · Learn the cost of overextension

Three frigates captured Caldera on 20. Khar immediately counterattacked, destroyed the entire fleet—including Last Light—and recaptured the world. The player cancelled an exposed unfinished laboratory, recovering its unspent materials, rebuilt five frigates, researched shields and retook Caldera on 29. Khar’s offered peace paid 60 credits and secured a five-cycle truce. A subsequent legal scout visit observed seven Khar frigates at Stillwater: accepting settlement had bought valuable breathing room.

33–42 · A trade corridor becomes a war front

Veyr gave notice to end trade on 33; borders closed on 35 and the visiting frigate withdrew as advertised. Veyr declared war in the following rival phase. Sable fell on 38, yielding an intact Extraction Charter and roughly 20 minerals per cycle. Its counterattack nearly destroyed the occupying fleet. On 39, two paid emergency repairs and a deliberate attack saved the foothold. Hesper required a second invasion volley on 40 after its first defense held at one point.

43–50 · Convert a foothold into capital conquest

A new shipyard at Sable made forward cruiser production practical. Two cruisers cleared Aster, then Veyr Prime’s successive frigate defenders. Distributed Command enabled an orbital engagement and capital invasion in the same cycle 46. The player accepted a fresh Veyr peace offer after capturing the capital, leaving a garrison and consolidating. At cycle 50: nine worlds, two capitals, four cruisers, eight frigates and one scout. This was the explicit milestone before continuing to a final result.

52–57 · Win before the network aligns

Five cruisers defeated eight Khar frigates at Stillwater on 52, losing two cruisers. The survivors captured Kharos on 53. Four Caldera frigates were split into two pairs: one held the frontier, one moved to garrison the captured capital, later reinforced locally. The player declared war on the Choir before entering its territory, losing trade income. Three Choir frigates intercepted at Carina; capturing that world on 55 enabled 30 minerals of immediate repairs before continuing. The expedition bypassed Nyx, cleared a frigate at Seraph and captured undefended Lumen on 57. Two reserve cruisers were still behind the main force.

Which decisions had weight

  • Minerals and production were real early constraints. The visible cycle-33 treasury had only 13 minerals; new construction was deferred. A forward shipyard reduced reinforcement travel. On cycle 47, a four-cycle Forge Charter would delay the next cruiser, so direct production was chosen instead.
  • Command changed the operational tempo. Warships gaining a second move shortened reinforcement routes and allowed a battle plus invasion on cycle 46. This was a meaningful research payoff rather than an incremental statistic.
  • Repair location mattered. Emergency repairs at contested Sable rescued a damaged survivor while enemy presence blocked passive repair. At Carina, conquest created a place to spend minerals on immediate hull recovery before the final march.
  • Splitting was useful for commitments, not free power. The cycle-29 split apportioned damaged hull and retained zero movement. The next passive repair pool remained four hull total, shared 2.4/1.6 between the formations. On 53, division let the player hold two worlds while the cruisers moved on.
  • Peace changed the map without ending the campaign. Khar’s settlement protected the first recovered foothold. Veyr’s later settlement preserved a captured capital and released the offensive force for another theater. Both truces were honored.
  • Discovery memory survived the war. Caldera’s observatory was preserved on 29, but its required laboratory only completed on 43 because military production intervened. The mature discovery on 45 offered a permanent restoration or an immediate atlas; publishing 140 science completed Command. A delayed local story became a timely operational choice.

Faction pressure, and what the win does not prove

Khar punished a lightly defended invasion, maintained a substantial observed frigate force and made the second offensive costly. Veyr withdrew commercial access, initiated war, counterattacked Sable twice and rebuilt individual capital defenders. The Choir expanded through a foreign war, captured Carina and completed three beacon sites while the player was fighting. Its interception at Carina cost cruiser hull; its frigate at Seraph killed the scout. These rivals produced distinct practical problems during this run.

After those field forces were defeated, the final capital assaults were short. Lumen had no local defender when the cruisers arrived. This alone does not justify stronger arbitrary garrisons, hidden-information defenses or a guaranteed last-minute contest. The visible evidence supports reviewing how a faction communicates and prioritizes threatened capitals after losing its field army; a balance change would need its own controlled test.

The late treasury surplus did not make the middle game trivial. The player had deliberately stopped marginal civilian construction while finishing a war. The final technology was still incomplete, and the game ended before an empty post-research phase. This run gives no reason to add generic spending programs merely to consume the final credits.

Friction and two priorities

1. Preserve fleet intent in readiness and selection. Deliberate garrisons repeatedly appeared in next-ready cycling and end-cycle reminders. By cycle 53 the compact fleet bar showed the four older garrisons while the active cruisers required opening the roster. The useful improvement is explicit Hold/Resume plus an active-mission-first view: held garrisons stay inspectable, genuine threats can still notify, and a continuing route remains easy to resume. This campaign supplies evidence for the separately implemented Stage 11 control; that newer UI was not tested here.

2. Make combat participation clear before the order. At Sable in the cycle 41 rival phase, three player frigates fought while a colocated full-health cruiser remained untouched. Two frigates were lost. The report correctly described the engaged formations, but the local fleet list had suggested a combined defensive presence. Show which formation is eligible or selected to defend, and explicitly explain that colocated formations do not combine automatically. Retain the current damage and merge rules until a separate tactical-design review; clarity would have improved this decision without a balance buff.

Secondary friction was diplomatic: unsolicited AI trade in v0.10 opened both borders, and a binding peace offer could coexist with prose rejecting a hypothetical new proposal. Both directly affected planning and confidence. These support the separate consent and offer-wording work already underway; they are not reasons to alter peace willingness thresholds.

Corrections retained with the evidence

  • The Battle report button was working. The failed cycle-41/42 attempts used invalid CSS such as [data-report=11]. Quoting the numeric value worked; the corrected report screenshot is retained. The client was changed to print automation errors visibly. The original failed attempts remain in the receipt log.
  • The refugee “cap” concern was a misunderstanding. At cycle 47, the player chose supplies because a capital at 8/8 appeared unable to benefit from another inhabitant. Independent source review confirmed that the scripted welcome reward can increase population beyond normal capacity. No lost-reward bug is claimed, and the actual alternate choice was not revised.
  • The cycle-29 peace contradiction was presentation, not an invalid settlement. Capturing Caldera reduced current Khar peace willingness, while its already-issued offer remained binding. Exact replay reproduced that change. The refusal text described a new proposal; accepting the pending settlement was legitimate.
  • Browser closures are not attributed to the game. The run recorded no page exceptions. An initial browser disconnection, the cycle-31 process interruption and a post-victory closure are preserved as tooling/environment events. Failed selectors and modal-covered controls are also recorded, rather than reported as broken game buttons.

Reproduce the result

The portable bundle contains the exact pinned rules-engine graph, normalized commands with original annotations and UI receipts, unchanged exports, compressed original observation logs, build metadata and SHA-256 hashes. Run:

node replay/replay.mjs

The runner recreates the seed, applies all 340 recorded commands, checks all 14 export events against the actual downloads, validates nonnegative resources and save shape after every command, and repeats every action from a JSON-reloaded state. The final state matches in every serialized field, including RNG, fleets, observations and history. This is an offline rules-engine verification of the UI campaign, not a claim that the runner replays browser pixels.
